parameters: \n<Florante's Father> now you will learn in full what
it is.
\n<Florante's Father> Three hundred years. Your family,
my family — every Filipino — born under the law of
another country.
\n<Florante's Father>We pay taxes to live on our own
land. We work to enrich men we did not choose and do
not want. No right to complain. No voice. No freedom
to choose.
\n<Florante's Father>The Katipunan is the answer to
that. It was built by men who decided that endurance
was over.
\n<Florante's Father> The purpose: freedom. Real
freedom
\n<Florante's Father> not for a few chosen men, but
for every child of the Philippines. Its members are
not officials or rich men
\n<Florante's Father>they are farmers, laborers, men
like your father and mine.
\n<Florante's Father> Their leadership rests on one
man: Andres Bonifacio. You will meet him today.
\n<Florante's Father> This day is not ordinary. We are
here because something is about to happen. And after
this day, there is no going back to how things were.
\m[1] \fi He said Andres Bonifacio. He said today. I
know what today is. I know what is about to happen.
\m[1] \fi I've read about it. But knowing about
something and standing inside it are two completely
different things. And right now I am very, very much
inside it.
\m[1]\fi That's him!
\m[1]\fi That's Andres Bonifacio. Not a portrait. Not
a statue. He is thirty-two years old and he is standing
twelve feet away from me and the revolution
\m[1]\fi the actual Philippine Revolution — begins
today. Today. While I am standing in this room.
\n<Andres Bonifacio> Brothers.
\n<Andres Bonifacio>Many of us have waited. Waited for
change to come through prayer, through petition,
through peaceful means.
\n<Andres Bonifacio>Waited for men of influence to
speak for us. Waited for justice to be given to us by
the men who hold power.
\n<Andres Bonifacio>But justice is not given by the
powerful to the powerless. Three hundred years are the
proof.
\n<Andres Bonifacio>Our freedom as a nation will not be
received as a gift. It will be taken. It will be fought
for. And now, on this day, the fight begins.
\n<Andres Bonifacio>I am not asking if you are ready.
Because I already know the answer. You are here.
You came. Courage is not taken — it is already in us.
Always.
\n<Andres Bonifacio>The one question I still ask you
today is this
\n<Andres Bonifacio>Are you ready to make a promise?
\n<Andres Bonifacio>Not to me.
\n<Andres Bonifacio>not to the Katipunan
\n<Andres Bonifacio>but to your countrymen, to your
children, to all who come after you
\n<Andres Bonifacio>Are you ready to sign?
\n<Andres Bonifacio>not on paper
\n<Andres Bonifacio>but in your own blood?
\fi Half an hour later
\n<Andres Bonifacio>We have ourselves some
new faces
\n<Andres Bonifacio> What are your names?

\n<Andres Bonifacio> Take this knife, take a small cut

\n<Andres Bonifacio> Now, you two are officially an
